Radar plot comparison of averaged industry START values This visualization shows different results than LDA alone. Suitability commands a high score for both corpora, but concepts such as short-term cost show a decline in ranking, therefore justifying the need for employing metrics other than saliency alone. Whereas saliency lacks the ability to pick up on contextual references, the c-TF-IDF is particularly able to understand context due to its learned relationships between words when placed together, or in the same sentence. By combining these metrics into the START metric, we can represent both the “commonness” of the topics, and their contextual importance within the literature. Discussion START Costs and Benefits This paper introduces START as a more comprehensive text mining metric of performance that allows for some new and meta-algorithmic uses of diverse language models. Using a diversity of methods (such as the LDA and BERTopic methods exemplified here), allows for different components of natural language to be captured, and for new uses of natural language processing (NLP) to be developed. For example, there are many clustering metrics used in NLP (coherence, silhouette score) that are focused on identifying the most similar topics. These metrics have value in distilling or summarizing a corpus, in building key words libraries, and in assessing sentiment. The benefits of the proposed START methods and metric is that they allow practitioners to understand how important their pre-determined topics of interest are in a corpus. START provides practitioners with a metric to quantify these areas of interest by ranking them from lowest to highest importance. In this study, we have defined topics of interest on the basis of both theories of technology adoption, and the applied literature on MDHD vehicle adoption. By defining corpora of interest and applying the START metric, we can assess the relative importance of these predefined topics 88 Bradley, T.H., et al., Agent-Based, Bottom-Up Medium- and Heavy-duty Electric Vehicle Economics, Operation, Charging and Adoption, Final Technical Report, DE-EE0009664 experimentally, allowing for direct comparison of the importance of those topics among various corpora (i.e. the academic and industry corpora), and for inputting those of importance into subsequent simulation and analysis.
